title: Towards an AI-Augmented Textbook
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the longstanding limitation of textbooks as largely static, one-size-fits-all learning materials. The authors investigate whether generative AI can transform textbook content into a more personalized, multimodal, and pedagogically effective learning experience while preserving fidelity to the source material. The paper also asks whether such an AI-augmented textbook can improve learning outcomes compared with standard digital textbook reading.

The intervention is Learn Your Way, an experimental system built by Google’s LearnLM team. It applies a two-step generation process: first, textbook text is personalized to learner attributes such as grade level and personal interests; second, the personalized content is transformed into multiple representations, including immersive text, slides with optional narration, audio lessons, mind maps, timelines, memory aids, visual illustrations, embedded questions, and quizzes. The system is designed to support personalization, learner agency, multiple representations of knowledge, and formative assessment.

The empirical work includes two parts. First, pedagogical experts evaluated generated components across 10 OpenStax textbook sources, multiple grade levels, and learner interest profiles using a detailed pedagogy rubric. Second, the paper reports a randomized controlled trial with 60 students aged 15–18 from the Chicago area, recruited across urban, suburban, and rural schools. Participants were randomly assigned either to Learn Your Way or to a control condition using a standard digital reader (Adobe Acrobat Reader) to study the same LibreTexts chapter on adolescent brain development. They then completed an immediate assessment, a survey, qualitative interview, and a delayed retention assessment three days later.

The main conclusion is that students using Learn Your Way outperformed those using the standard digital reader on both the immediate and delayed retention assessments, with statistically significant differences reported for both. Students also rated the AI-augmented tool more positively across multiple learning-experience measures. Expert evaluations suggested that most generated components had high pedagogical value, though visual illustration was weaker than other components. The authors conclude that generative AI can meaningfully augment textbooks and improve learning efficacy, while noting that future work is needed to determine which components drive the effects and to test the system across more topics and settings.

identified_tools.name: Learn Your Way
identified_tools.description: An experimental AI-augmented textbook learning experience that transforms source textbook content into personalized text, multiple representations (e.g., slides, audio lessons, mind maps, immersive text), and formative assessments. It is built using Gemini-based generation and additional image-model fine-tuning for educational illustrations.
identified_tools.use_case: Studied as a personalized textbook-learning system for secondary students, compared against a standard digital reader while students learned an unfamiliar textbook chapter and completed immediate and delayed assessments.

findings.finding_summary: In a randomized study, students using Learn Your Way scored higher than students using a Digital Reader on the Immediate Assessment after learning an unfamiliar textbook chapter. The difference was statistically significant (p = 0.03); 60 students aged 15–18 participated, randomly assigned 30 per condition. No effect size was reported.
findings.measure: Immediate post-learning assessment score on an expert-written assessment covering the chapter

findings.finding_summary: Students using Learn Your Way also outperformed the Digital Reader group on a delayed Retention Assessment administered three days later. The difference was statistically significant (p = 0.03); 58 of 60 participants completed the retention assessment. No effect size was reported.
findings.measure: Delayed retention assessment score three days after the learning session

findings.finding_summary: Post-study survey results favored Learn Your Way across all reported learning-experience items. For example, 100% vs. 70% agreed the tool made them more comfortable taking the assessment, 93% vs. 67% wanted to use it in the future, 90% vs. 57% found it enjoyable, and 83% vs. 40% said it would make them more effective at learning than tools they currently use; figure notes these differences were significant at p < .05. Item-level sample sizes were n=30 per condition.
findings.measure: Learner self-report survey on comfort, understanding, future use, recommendation, enjoyment, perceived performance, and perceived learning effectiveness

identified_tools.name: Gemini
identified_tools.description: Google’s large language model family used here as the core generative engine for textbook re-leveling, personalization, content transformation, assessment generation, and interactive lesson generation.
identified_tools.use_case: Used as the underlying model powering Learn Your Way’s text personalization, slides, narration, audio lessons, mind maps, mnemonics, embedded questions, and quizzes; also used in expert-rated pedagogical evaluations of generated components.

findings.finding_summary: Pedagogical experts rated the overall Learn Your Way experience generated largely with Gemini at over 0.90 across evaluation axes, and all components received relatively high pedagogy values. The paper reports that Visual Illustration had the lowest scores among components, and that narrated slides scored notably higher on engagement than slides alone. These were expert rubric ratings rather than student learning outcomes, and no inferential statistics or effect sizes were reported.
findings.measure: Expert pedagogical rubric ratings of generated components and overall experience

quality_tier_rationale: The paper reports a randomized controlled comparison between Learn Your Way and a digital reader with n=60, plus delayed retention data, which is stronger than correlational evidence. However, effect sizes and confidence intervals are not reported, and the study appears limited to a single chapter/topic and modest sample size.
impact_tier_rationale: The direction of effects is positive and statistically significant for immediate and retention assessments, but the magnitude of impact is unclear because no effect sizes or confidence intervals are provided. Survey results also favor the intervention, but these are self-reports rather than standardized achievement effects.
